Press Council Of India

Press Council Of India - History, Mission, Composition, Chairman, Functions, Powers And More

Also Read Press Council Of India in Hindi
Download as PDF

Overview

Test Series

The Press Council of India (PCI) was formed in 1978 under the Press Council Act of 1978. It is an apex body for the regulation of the Press in the country. This body functions as an independent body. The Press Council of India is a statutory body formed under the Press Council of India Act of 1978. The Press Council of India has limited authority when it comes to addressing issues with a non-compliant newspaper or reporter. Its actions are confined to issuing warnings, admonishments, and censures. Essentially, the PCI predominantly serves in an advisory capacity, and it is the responsibility of the involved parties to comply with its recommendations.

Government departments are important from the relevance of the UPSC IAS Exams. This article will explain in detail about the Press Council of India, its composition, functions and powers from the perspective of civil service examination.

About Press Council of India

The Press Council of India was established in the year 1966 by the Parliament on the basis of the First Press Commission with the objective of preserving the freedom of the press and improving the standards of the press in India. The Press Council of India is governed by the Press Council of India Act of 1978. It is a quasi-judicial body that acts as a watchdog for the press and print media and looks into the violations of the guidelines. It functions as a regulatory body for the print media, defining and disseminating professional standards. Its mission is to protect press freedom and also preserve and develop the press standards in India. It adjudicates accusations of ethics violations and press freedom violations brought against and by the press, respectively. It is entrusted with the most important task of ensuring the Freedom of Expression enshrined in the Constitution.

Mission of PCI

The Press Council of India's mission is to safeguard the independence of newspapers and news agencies. It aims to establish a code of conduct for these entities and journalists, aligning with elevated professional standards. The Council endeavors to ensure that newspapers, news agencies, and journalists uphold high standards of public taste while maintaining a balance between rights and responsibilities. It actively monitors developments that could impede the supply and dissemination of news of public interest, striving to promote a harmonious relationship among those involved in newspaper or news agency production and publication. Additionally, the Council addresses concerns related to the concentration of ownership and other factors that may impact the independence of the press.

Appointment of PCI Chairman

The following people select the chairman of the Press Council of India:

  • Speaker of Lok Sabha
  • Chairman of Rajya Sabha
  • One member of the PCI.

Funding of Press Council of India

The Press Council of India is funded by the revenue collected by it as the fee levied on the registered newspapers on the basis of their circulation. It does not levy a fee on newspapers which have a circulation of less than 5000 copies.

Check out the article on Election Commission Of India for UPSC Exam.

Recent News

The Ministry of Information and Broadcasting has issued the 2021 Information Technology (Guidelines For Intermediaries And Digital Media Ethics Code) Rules, commonly referred to as the new Digital Media Rules. These regulations impose specific responsibilities on digital news publishers, requiring them to adhere to a code of ethics aligned with the norms of journalistic conduct established by the Press Council of India and the Programme Code outlined in the Cable Television Network Act.

Composition Of Press Council of India

The composition of the Press Council of India are:

PCI is led by a chairman who has, by convention, been a retired judge of the Supreme Court of India.

Apart from the Chairman, the PCI also consists of 28 members, out of which 20 represent the Press and are represented by the press agencies. The members are-

  • Two Members of the Rajya Sabha
  • Three members of the Lok Sabha
  • 7 Working Journalists (other than newspaper editors)
  • 6 Newspaper Editors
  • 3 Person having extensive knowledge of Public Affairs.
  • 1 Person in charge of the News Organization
  • 6 Persons engaged in the business of managing newspapers

The members serve for a term of three years.

A retiring member of the Council is eligible for renomination for not more than one term (max 2 consecutive years).

Functions of Press Council Of India

The functions of the Press Council of India are:

  • Keep an eye on anything that can restrict the free flow of information or news.
  • Create a code of conduct for Journalists to ensure high professional standards.
  • To create a code of conduct for news agencies to maintain high professional standards.
  • Providing training to new journalists.
  • One of its goals is to encourage technical and other news-related research.
  • To make sure that newspapers continue to operate independently.
  • To ensure good news quality for the general public.

Powers of Press Council Of India

The powers of the Press Council of India are:

  • PCI is responsible for enquiring about the complaints it receives.
  • It can also summon witnesses and demand copies of public records.
  • PCI can issue warnings criticize the guilty, be it the journalist, newspaper, newspaper agency or editor.
  • Decisions taken by the Press Council of India are final and cannot be appealed before a court of law.
  • Any editor or journalist can complain to the Press Council of India (PCI) about professional misconduct or violation of journalistic ethics by an editor or journalist.

Limitations of the Powers of Press Council Of India

Two main factors that restrict the powers of the Press Council of India. They are:

  • While enforcing the guidelines laid down to ensure press freedom, it has limited powers to ensure its application. It cannot penalize anyone for the violation of the guidelines.
  • It only has powers to enforce standards on the print media. The powers of the Press Council of India are restricted with respect to electronic media like Radio, television and the Internet. Its powers are restricted to Journals, magazines and newspapers.

Complaint Procedure in Press Council of India

  • Under Section 14 of PCI, anyone can file a complaint with the Press Council against a newspaper, editor, or journalist.
  • The complaint arises when there is a breach of recognized ethical standards in the publication or non-publication of news, articles, cartoons, or advertisements.
  • Initially, the complainant must write to the editor, highlighting the objectionable content and giving them a chance to address and rectify the matter.
  • If satisfied, the complaint concludes at this stage; however, if dissatisfied, the complainant can escalate the matter to the Press Council.
  • The complaint submitted to the Press Council must include details like the name and address of the editor, journalist, or newspaper involved and specify how the content is objectionable under the Press Council Act, 1978.
  • Additionally, relevant particulars, copies of correspondence with the editor, and a declaration that no legal proceedings are pending must be provided.
  • According to the Press Council (Procedure for Inquiry) Regulations, 1979, complaints against dailies, news agencies, and weeklies must be filed within two months, while in all other cases, it must be done within four months.

Conclusion

The Press Council of India, established with goodwill, prefers irresponsible media over controlled media. The Council is dedicated to preserving the freedom and independence of the press, guided by constitutional principles. Newspapers are now filled with advertisements and page 3 news, witnessing a significant decline in content capacity. PCI acknowledges its responsibility for this decline and recognizes that it needs more authority. Despite having more teeth than byte, PCI struggles with a considerable backlog and often fails to dispose of cases on time. In the case of Ajay Goswami v. Union of India (2007) 1 SCC 143, the Press Council admitted its lack of punitive power to ensure compliance with its directions.

Press Council of India FAQs

What is the role of the Press Council of India?

The Press Council of India acts as a watchdog of the press. It adjudicates the complaints against the press for violation of ethics and also for freedom of press respectively.
